evidence: app/package.json:14 — nitro ^3.0.261029-rc, a release-candidate build (published 2026-10-29), is the app's only pre-release dependency
app/vite.config.ts:5 — nitro() Vite plugin from nitro/vite, the RC Nitro v3 API
app/package.json:13 — vite ^8.3.5, stable only since 2026-03-12 (Rolldown bundler swap), in a central place
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].jsx:138, app/src/lib/data.js:118 — all data/routing source code uses only long-stable query/createAsync/'use server' APIs; grep finds zero unstable_/experimental_ names
reach.rationale: No experimental source-level APIs at all, but the deployment foundation rests on one RC dependency (Nitro v3) plus recently-stable Vite 8 and router 1.0 in central places — the RC is mandated by the framework's current stable release, which tempers the risk.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:1-7 — the entire RC surface is a 3-line config in the officially documented form; nothing else references nitro
app/src/lib/data.js:118 — app logic only uses stable @solidjs/router query primitives
app/package.json:6 — npm start runs node .output/server/index.mjs, avoiding Nitro v3's experimental 'nitro serve' runtime mode
containment.rationale: The single pre-release dependency is fully contained in the build config; swapping Nitro v3 RC for its eventual stable release would touch two files and zero application source.

evidence: app/package.json:14 — nitro@3 RC pin matches the official SolidStart v2 migration guide (docs.solidjs.com/solid-start/v2/migrating-from-v1: 'npm i @solidjs/start@2 @solidjs/router@1 nitro@3 vite@8', 'Use Nitro v3's own nitro() plugin from nitro/vite')
app/package.json:17 — engines node>=24 matches SolidStart v2's documented Node requirement
app/vite.config.ts:3-6 — solidStart() with default options; the app does not opt into the new 2.1.0 'ssr: "data-only"' mode or Nitro RC runtime mode it doesn't need
justification.rationale: The one experimental reach is exactly what the framework's current stable release requires — there is no stable alternative — and no experimental feature is used gratuitously.

findings.issue: nitro is pinned as ^3.0.261029-rc — Nitro v3 is still a release candidate (stable is v2.13.5), each RC iteration ships breaking changes, and a caret pin on a date-versioned RC floats across future RC builds
findings.suggestion: This pin is unavoidable for SolidStart v2, but consider pinning an exact RC (no caret) and adding a CI check for build+start after each nitro RC bump; migrate promptly when Nitro v3 goes stable

findings.issue: h3 ^2.0.1-rc.26 ships transitively under Nitro v3, so the production server runtime includes RC HTTP-layer code
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change in app code (h3 is never imported directly); just be aware that RC-level churn in h3 v2 is covered by the nitro bump policy above

findings.issue: vite ^8.3.5 — Vite 8 has only been stable since 2026-03-12 and replaced the bundler with Rolldown, a large architectural change with a fast patch cadence in its first weeks
findings.suggestion: Stable and correct for SolidStart v2; keep the lockfile updated to pick up the Vite 8 patch line and watch the changelog for plugin-ecosystem regressions

summary: The application code itself uses zero experimental APIs — every route, component and data function is built on long-stable SolidStart/Solid primitives, with no unstable names or flags anywhere in src. The only pre-release dependency is nitro v3 (RC), but that is precisely what the current stable SolidStart v2 requires and it is confined to a three-line vite.config that follows the official migration guide. Risk is therefore low and well-contained: the main exposure is RC-iteration churn in the build/runtime layer, not in app source.
